title: An Edison Volunteer’s Passion for Fighting Food Insecurity

body_markdown:
As a little girl growing up in India, some of Prabha Cadambi’s earliest memories are of watching her mother go out of her way to give back to the community.


“My mom was a champion of helping children,” said Cadambi, an advisor in Business Controls for Customer Service at Southern California Edison. “We lived in an area that was always in need, so my mom would constantly organize ways to help.”


When Cadambi moved to the States and started working at SCE, the first thing she did was seek out[opportunities to get involved](https://www.sce.com/about-sce/community) .


At the National Family Volunteer event, different corporations engage in friendly competition, hoping to be the company that packs the most boxes.


PHOTO CREDIT: Taylor Hillo


In her nearly 40 years at the company, Cadambi has spent countless hours volunteering with SCE, helping various nonprofits across Southern California. Even now, she dedicates two Saturdays a month to working with community-based organizations.


An event she never misses:[National Family Volunteer Day](https://nationaltoday.com/family-volunteer-day/) at the[Community Action Partnership of Orange County](https://www.capoc.org/) (CAP OC), Edison’s largest annual volunteer opportunity.


Every year, different corporations bring their friends and families to help pack boxes of nonperishables for community members in need. The companies use the day of service as an opportunity to give back while showcasing their competitive sides — each hoping to pack the most boxes.


“I enjoy the camaraderie, and of course the competition,” said Cadambi, who has attended the event for more than 10 years. “You feel pride in wearing the yellow Edison shirt. We are part of the community and here to serve the community.”


National Family Volunteer Day is Edison's largest annual volunteer event.


PHOTO CREDIT: Taylor Hillo


This year, 240 Edison volunteers and their families packed 3,920 boxes, helping push the event’s overall total to 17,181 boxes.


“Every box represents an older adult who will have access to nutritious food because of the care and effort of volunteers that participate each year,” said Megan Day, philanthropy director of CAP OC.


While California food banks are where Cadambi offers up most of her time, her passion to fight food insecurity started when she volunteered with a local church, packing backpacks with near-expired food for kids who didn't have access to meals outside of school.


“The food that went into those backpacks was pathetic,” she said. “It was devastating to see. After that, I made a point to make myself available for anything related to food security. A child should never go hungry.”


More than 240 Edison volunteers packed a total of 3,920 boxes of food on National Family Volunteer Day.


PHOTO CREDIT: Taylor Hillo


Cadambi passed along her mother’s passion for volunteering to her own kids too. For years of their childhood, she brought her three kids to every event, including National Family Volunteer Day.


Now, as adults and spread out between Orange County, Los Angeles and New York, it can be tougher to volunteer as a family.


But even from different cities, Cadambi’s kids make a point to continue the legacy started by their mother — her son even sitting on the board of Best Buddies, an organization dedicated to ending the isolation of those with disabilities.


“My entire family is invested in volunteering,” Cadambi said. “Even my niece who goes to USC invites me to volunteer events. And as soon as my grandson is old enough, I'll get him volunteering too.”


***For more information on Edison International’s commitment to giving back, visit*[edison.com/community](https://www.edison.com/community) .**
